note: Title page, preface and contents (cover: Piprahwa caskets).
Chandavaram stupa (Amaravati idiom); Antichak = Vikramaśīla (not in the Xiyu ji); no Xiyu ji place.
Exploration in Chhattisgarh (brick temples like Sirpur); no location argued.
Bhokardan (Bhogavardhana) excavation; Ajanta mentioned only as a road; not a Xiyu ji location.

author: K. M. Srivastava, Lalchand Singh, Birendra Nath, D. P. Sinha, Mid-eastern Circle, Archaeological Survey of India
asr_identification: Piprahwa (and its immediate neighbourhood), District Basti, Uttar Pradesh
evidence: 1972-73: 31 terracotta sealings in Brahmi of 1st-2nd c. A.D. from a verandah of the eastern monastery at Piprahwa, one legend reading "Om Devaputra Vihare Kapilavastu Bhikshu Sanghasa"; quadrangular monastery of 33 cells; stupa section shows three building stages; NBP, punch-marked, Kushan and Ayodhya coins
quote: This year's excavation resulted in the discovery of thirty-one terracotta sealings, giving a clue to the location of ancient Kapilavastu, the capital of the Sakyas…one reading Om Devaputra Vihare Kapilavastu Bhikshu Sanghasa…It could be inferred therefrom that the ancient city of Kapilavastu must be in the immediate neighbourhood of the stupa and the monastery.
note: The key inscribed find: the sealings name the monastery of the Kapilavastu sangha, and the excavators infer that the city lay next to Piprahwa. This moves Kapilavastu from Tilaurakot (Nepal Tarai), Mizutani's identification, to Piprahwa-Ganwaria (India). Mizutani follows the older view; the 1972-73 find is not reflected in it. The sealings date to the Kushan period, so they show the name for the monastery (the Kapilavastu sangha), not necessarily the 7th-century city that Xuanzang saw.
Sonkh (Mathura) level table; Sarai Nahar Rai; no Xiyu ji location.

author: S. R. Das, Department of Archaeology, University of Calcutta
evidence: 1972-73 season: many inscribed terracotta seals and sealings from the intermediate levels; five with dharmachakra and deer, one reading "Sri Raktamrittika Mahavihara[ry]a-bhikshu Sanghasya"; monastery walls, Phases II-VI
quote: The excavation yielded a large number of antiquities, including many complete and fragmentary inscribed terracotta seals and sealings of various shapes and sizes…One of the seals contains the legend: Sri Raktatnrittikd Mahdvihd-rakaryabhikshu Sanghasya.
note: Inscribed seal naming the Raktamṛttikā mahāvihāra, found at Rajbadidanga (near Rangamati). This confirms Mizutani's location of 絡多末知僧伽藍 at Rāṅgāmāṭi and, through it, Karṇasuvarṇa nearby. The identification is stated explicitly in passage 289.

author: S. R. Das, Department of Archaeology, University of Calcutta
evidence: Several inscribed seals bearing Raktamrittika legends; three cultural periods, c. 4th-5th to 11th-12th c. A.D.
quote: The discovery of several inscribed seals bearing Raktamrittika legends lends further support to the identification of the Raktamrittika monastery of Hiuen Tsang's accounts with the present site of Rajbadidanga, now under excavation.
note: Explicit confirmation, by excavation, of the Xuanzang identification. It agrees with Mizutani (Rāṅgāmāṭi; Rajbadidanga lies in the Rangamati area). The occupation (4th-5th to 11th-12th c.) covers Xuanzang's date. 1972-73 report.
Epigraphy: Jaina inscriptions (Mathura anvaya); no location.
Epigraphy: Mathura inscriptions (vihara of Bodhisattva); no location.
Indo-Sassanian coins from Sarnath; radiocarbon dates.
Preservation of monuments; the "stupa and monastery of the Sakyas, Piprahwa" is only cleared and repaired, with no identification argued.
Amaravati stupa excavation (structural phases); no Xiyu ji location argued.
Chandavaram; Antichak (Vikramaśīla); no Xiyu ji location.
Explorations in Gaya district (Barabar sculptures re-examined); Balirajgarh; no location.
Malhar excavation (route from Kausambi); no location.

author: K. M. Srivastava, Excavations Branch (I), Nagpur, Archaeological Survey of India
asr_identification: Piprahwa and the adjacent mound Ganwaria, District Basti, Uttar Pradesh
evidence: 1974-75: eastern monastery at Piprahwa in four phases (plan changes between phases II and III), a few more terracotta sealings; at Ganwaria two massive baked-brick complexes with entrances to the east, the larger c. 39 m square with 25-26 rooms round a courtyard, five phases
quote: EXCAVATION AT PIPRAHWA AND GANWARIA, DISTRICT BASTI.—In continuation of the earlier work (1973-74, pp. 27-28), the Excavations Branch (I), Nagpur, under Shri K. M. Srivastava, resumed excavation at Piprahwa, and at the adjacent mound, Ganwaria…The excavation yielded a few terracotta sealings and iron door sockets, hooks and hinges.
note: Fieldwork continuing the Piprahwa = Kapilavastu programme. The interpretation (Ganwaria as the Sakya palace) follows in passage 304. Bears on Mizutani's Tilaurakot only through that claim. The explorations in the same passage along the Rapti "from Sravasti" have nothing on location.

author: K. M. Srivastava, Excavations Branch (I), Nagpur, Archaeological Survey of India
asr_identification: Ganwaria (residential complex) beside Piprahwa, District Basti, Uttar Pradesh
evidence: Ganwaria: Periods I-III (pre-NBP, NBP, Kushan); terracotta sealings, figurines, silver punch-marked coin, terracotta Buddha head, decorated horse at the entrance of the larger complex; complexes face away from the stupa, unlike the Piprahwa monasteries
quote: The proximity to the ancient site of Piprahwa, where the sealings with the legend Kapilavastu were found, the impressive structures, and the large quantity of antiquities hardly leave any doubt that they were the residential complex of the chief of the capital town of Kapilavastu, i.e. Sakya king Suddhodhana and his predecessors.
note: Builds on the 1972-73 sealings (passage 286): Ganwaria is taken as the Sakya palace, so Kapilavastu = Piprahwa-Ganwaria. This differs from Mizutani (Tilaurakot). The palace label is an inference from size and closeness to Piprahwa; no inscription names the complex.
Exploration at Kannauj (Club Ghar Teela); no identification argued; Gorakhpur site list.
Mathura excavation (Dhulkot); no Xiyu ji location.
Mathura, Kankali Tila tank (Jaina); no Xiyu ji location.
Preservation of monuments (Kolhua, Nalanda, Kumrahar etc.).

author: Vijaya Kant Misra, Mid-eastern Circle, Archaeological Survey of India
name_in_asr: Sarai Mound, Nalanda (temple of king Purnavarman's bronze Buddha)
asr_identification: Sarai Mound temple near the excavated remains at Nalanda, District Nalanda, Bihar
evidence: 1975-76: rectangular brick temple 31.70 x 22.70 m with projecting arms, painted stone pedestal in the garbhagriha, votive stupas, Buddha images, sealings; an earlier find there was a 7th-8th c. inscription mentioning bronze Buddha images installed by king Purnavarman
quote: It may be recalled here that an inscription of the seventh-eighth century A.D., mentioning the bronze images of Buddha, being installed by king Pumavarman, also corroborated by the description by Hieun Tsang, was discovered at the site earlier.
note: new: the copper (bronze) Buddha image of king Pūrṇavarman (滿冑王), c. 80 ft high in a six-storeyed pavilion, which the Xiyu ji places near Nālandā. It has no row of its own in the master table (nearest: 09.03.01). The excavators identify the Sarai Mound temple with it on the strength of the inscription. Consistent with Mizutani's Nālandā = Bargaon ruins.
Kasital, Raja Karna-ka-Qila; Ahichchhatra only as a pottery type.

author: K. M. Srivastava, Excavations Branch (I), Nagpur, Archaeological Survey of India
evidence: 1975-76: house-complexes beside the larger structural complex; a block of rooms, verandahs and two courtyards interpreted as a school; four shrines, one octagonal with many terracotta Buddha heads; disc with elephant, lion and bull like an Asokan abacus
quote: This structure-complex appears to have been a school, which would corroborate the statement of the Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang.
note: Part of the argument that Ganwaria-Piprahwa is Kapilavastu (passages 286, 304). It differs from Mizutani (Tilaurakot). The report does not say which statement of Xuanzang it means. The Xiyu ji's Kapilavastu has the Bodhisattva's study-hall site (太子受業之處), probably what is meant.
Ganwaria finds; Salargarh monastery 200 m E of Piprahwa (Kushan); no identification argued (see 304, 321).
Mathura excavation periods; no Xiyu ji location.
Mathura, Katra mound inner fortification; no location.
Epigraphy, Andhra (Amaravati Mahavinaseliya, Alluru Purvasaila sect); does not locate a Xiyu ji place.
Coins; Sarnath sealings with the Buddhist creed; no location.
Afghanistan explorations (Begram) and Bamiyan Buddha conservation; no location argued.
Andhra excavations (Nelakondapally, Agiripalli); Nagarjunakonda for comparison only.
Katragarh; Kolhua stupa and Lion Pillar excavation (structural phases); no identification argued.

author: K. M. Srivastava, Excavations Branch (I), Nagpur, Archaeological Survey of India
asr_identification: Birdpur mound, 9 km south of Piprahwa, District Basti, Uttar Pradesh
evidence: 1976-77: circular mound with a modern linga temple on top; two copper vessels at 6 m depth, one under a brick carved with an eight-petalled lotus; brick platform at 5.70 m; earlier stupa(?) of Kushan-Gupta date under a later square temple
quote: Birdpur, 9 km south of Piprahwa, which corroborates in distance and direction the recording of the Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang regarding the location of Sarakupa from Kapilavastu.
note: New identification of the Arrow-well (箭泉, Śarakūpa), which Mizutani leaves unlocated. It depends on taking Piprahwa as Kapilavastu: Xuanzang puts the well 30 li SE of the city, and Birdpur is about 9 km S of Piprahwa. The distance fits; the direction (S, not SE) is only roughly right. With Mizutani's Tilaurakot as the city it would not hold. No inscription was found.

author: K. M. Srivastava, Excavations Branch (I), Nagpur, Archaeological Survey of India
evidence: 1976-77: under Shrine 2 a test cut found rooms of a house-complex of phases I-III, i.e. shrines built over civic houses; Period III re-dated 2nd c. B.C. to the beginning of the Christian era, Period IV to the 4th c. A.D.; Kushan sealing "Kafu-puta Vimasa"
quote: In order to verify the observation of the Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang that civic structures were converted into religious structures, a small area on the north-western corner of Shrine 2 was undertaken for digging by removing an insignificant portion of the shrine. As expected, rooms of a house-complex, meant for common man, were encountered.
note: The dig was planned to test a Xuanzang statement. In Kapilavastu he describes vihāras and stupas built on the sites of the palace buildings (e.g. at the site of Śuddhodana's main hall). The excavators read the result as support for Ganwaria = Kapilavastu, which differs from Mizutani (Tilaurakot).
Ganwaria finds; Piprahwa stupa phases; Ayodhya excavation; no Xiyu ji identification argued.
Mathura (Dhanyavarma-vihara inscription); not a Xiyu ji place.
Satanikota excavation; no Xiyu ji place.
Nalanda Sarai Mound temple paintings (see 319); no identification argued this year.
Sringaverpur excavation; no Xiyu ji place.
Treasure trove: Maitraka copper-plates from Vadnagar; does not argue Ānandapura.
Preservation (Jetavana, Sahet; Ganwaria and Piprahwa); no identification argued.
